title: Research dispatcher re-dispatched queued units twice on 2026-11-25 (RQ-FIX's stamp-race double-fire recurring): c7e3-01 runs 45525550688 (01:24Z) + 45527540463 (01:41Z), c7e3-02 runs 45537635254 (03:06Z) + 45541569251 (03:40Z); later runs cancelled by hand
note: Evidence: gh api actions/workflows/am-action-value.yml/runs (both pairs dispatched by github-actions[bot] from main, 17-34 min apart, the first still queued behind runner capacity). Likely cause: the stamp PR for the first dispatch (e.g. automation/research-queue-stamp-*, #28703 / #28700 open at the time) had not merged, so dispatch_queue._is_due saw last_dispatched_at null on the next hourly pass; long-queued workflow runs (am-action-value shards waited hours for runners) widen the window. Risk: two runs of a holdout-claiming unit double-append comms/research/holdout_reads.jsonl and burn runner time. clears_when: manual:dispatch_queue treats a unit with an in-progress or queued run of its workflow (research_unit input) as already dispatched, verified by a test; or row_state:RQ-FIX re-opened with this evidence. Filed by ML-PRIMARY (session_01AFoLuLpCY5gABbqk3EBUeV). [2026-11-25 06:29Z ML-PRIMARY] Third occurrence: c7e3-03 runs 45556426732 (05:51Z) + 45557781180 (~06:2xZ, cancelled by hand). Pattern holds: the first run sits queued behind runner capacity (am-action-value shards) and the next hourly pass re-dispatches. [2026-11-25 06:35Z manager, hypothesis, not yet verified] 3/3 c7e3 units double-fired today (c7e3-01, -02, -03; duplicates cancelled by ML-PRIMARY). scripts/research/dispatch_queue.py _is_due treats a cadence=once unit as due when it has no last_dispatched_at and no landed result; the in-flight window is meant to be covered by the open-stamp-PR check (pending_stamp_units, main()). Two suspects: (a) the am-action-value runs take hours, so the window outlives the stamp PR's life (merged or closed stamp PR, result not yet landed); (b) the stamp is refused: ML-PRIMARY reported 11-25 ~03:00Z that the decision-rule guard REFUSED last_dispatched_at stamps on new units (they reverted it in #28625), so for those units no stamp ever lands and every hourly run fires again until the result row lands. Check (b) first: diff the stamp PRs for c7e3-0N and grep the guard. Fix candidates: count an active workflow run for the unit (gh run list with the research_unit input) as in-flight, or let the guard accept a dispatcher-written stamp. Do after the reset. [2026-11-25 07:20Z ML-PRIMARY] Fourth: c7e3-04 runs 45565544762 (07:06Z) + 45566941882 (07:17Z, 11 min later, cancelled). The gap is shorter than an hour, so the re-dispatch is not only the hourly pass; two research-queue-dispatch runs were in progress at once (07:01Z and 07:09Z). [2026-11-25 09:15Z ML-PRIMARY] Second symptom, same class: STAMP-vs-GRADE race. The dispatcher re-stamped last_dispatched_at on already-run cadence-once units (1e06-10/11 at 06:02:51Z; their only runs were 05:04Z, 45551046958/45551051201, so stamped but NOT re-run; f1a0-14, f1a0-31 the same). The stamp and the grader's grading block both append at EOF of the unit YAML, so grader PR #28755 (run 45567748608) conflicted, waited 80 min and failed (commit-to-main failed_conflict); the older grader PR #28698 (run 45526199749) was dirty with guards red. ML-PRIMARY closed both as superseded (the grader is a deterministic function of committed results; E58 re-verifies) and dispatched research-queue-grade.yml on main at ~09:12Z for a fresh, conflict-free run. Also re-synced result PR #28766 (c7e3-03), which was dirty on a comms/research/holdout_reads.jsonl append conflict: union, ordered by read_at, check_pr_landing OK, holdout ledger tests pass. Fix candidates for the owner: the stamp step skips units whose result already exists on main or in an open result PR, or the grader rebases or retries instead of waiting 80 min on a conflict. [2026-11-25 10:00Z ML-PRIMARY] Fifth instance: RQ-20261125-a9d2-02 dispatched at 09:02:46Z (am-action-value 45581671996, kept) and AGAIN at 09:10:11Z (45582834336, cancelled at 09:59Z while still pending). That is 7.5 min apart, before the first run's last_dispatched_at stamp reached main, which matches the idempotence-on-unmerged-stamp mechanism. The fresh grader run 45582076674 landed cleanly (#28775 merged) and #28766 merged. 12:15Z evidence for the overlap hypothesis: research-queue-dispatch runs take ~36-37 min wall-clock (10:54->11:31, 11:02->11:39, 11:15->11:52, 11:31->12:08) and start every ~8-16 min, so ~3 runs are always in flight at once. Each run sees the same un-stamped due units before an earlier run's stamp lands -> double-fire. Fix candidates: a concurrency group on the workflow (cancel-in-progress:false, one group), or claim-before-dispatch. Main cost is probably the queued-runner backlog (391 queued runs at 12:14Z). [2026-11-25 14:20Z ML-PRIMARY] Sixth instance: RQ-20261125-c7e3-05 dispatched at 14:04:48Z (am-action-value 45630151734, kept) and again at 14:11:04Z (45631279875, cancelled while pending). The pattern is the same: a second dispatcher tick fires before the first stamp reaches main.
